feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong, credible CV for senior digital/public-sector communications roles: the experience progression is clear, the scope is substantial, and the profile aligns well with the target positioning. Writing is polished overall, but the document is somewhat dense and repetitive, with a few style/consistency issues that reduce sharpness.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear leadership narrative: strong progression at NACo from coordinator to director to consultant, which supports credibility and seniority.  
- Good impact signals: 10,000+ page migration, 3.5 million annual page views, 50+ internal publishers, and named tools/platforms add substance.  
- Broad, relevant expertise: combines strategy, governance, analytics, CMS/platform delivery, and multimedia in a way that fits enterprise digital leadership roles.

1. Top improvements  
- Reduce repetition across Header, Core Competencies, Topline Skills, Technical + IT, and Recent Projects; several themes and phrases recur too often. Consolidating would improve clarity and scannability.  
- Add more outcome-focused results beyond activity descriptions, especially for recent consulting work (e.g., efficiency gains, engagement lifts, adoption, search performance).  
- Fix style inconsistencies: “organization-wide” vs. “organization’s,” “front-end” vs. other hyphenation patterns, and list punctuation/formatting. Minor grammar/style edits: “social, and multimedia” should be “social and multimedia”; “Ranked among the top public universities...” is weak/irrelevant filler. No obvious misspellings or major typos found.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible intro with clear seniority and domain focus, but it’s slightly dense and repeats themes already covered in the subtitle, competencies, and work experience. Tightening it and adding one sharper differentiator will improve impact.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace “building the platforms” with more direct, outcome-oriented phrasing like “leading” or “modernizing” to sound more senior.
- Consider a tighter version: “Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience leading web modernization, governance, analytics, and content operations for high-volume public-sector communications. Builds scalable editorial systems, multimedia programs, and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.”
- If space allows, add a distinguishing scale cue from recent work, e.g. “10,000+ page websites” or “enterprise publishing environments.”
- Keep parallel style consistent: “web modernization, analytics, editorial systems, multimedia, and AI-enabled experiences.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Digital leader” overlaps with the subtitle “Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader.”
- “Governance models,” “content operations,” and “AI-enabled user experiences” are repeated in Core Competencies and recent experience.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block largely repeats the header and Topline Skills. Tightening the phrasing and making the categories more distinct will improve scan value and reduce overlap.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Use parallel noun phrases and sharpen wording: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, dashboarding, and reporting systems • Cross-channel communications leadership
- Replace broader/repetitive items with more specific strengths tied to recent work: AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integrations • Public-sector advocacy communications • Video, livestream, and studio operations
- Consider swapping “Multi-channel communications operations” to “Cross-channel communications leadership” to better reflect seniority.
- Standardize style by using “and” instead of “&” if the rest of the CV favors a more formal tone.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise website modernization,” “AI-enabled search,” “analytics infrastructure,” and “multimedia production” already appear in the header.
- This section also overlaps heavily with Topline Skills; keep competencies broader and let later sections carry the tools/details.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it reads dense and repeats themes already covered in Work Experience. Tightening phrasing and adding clearer outcomes or scope would make it more distinctive and impactful.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add dates or “Selected recent projects” framing to reinforce recency and context.
- Use parallel, tighter phrasing: start each item with a strong verb and reduce stacked nouns.
- Where possible, add one concrete result, audience, or scale marker instead of feature lists.
- Revise for consistency: use “10 x 20-foot” (not “10×20-foot”) and consider “AI-powered” or “AI-enabled” consistently across the CV.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI Hybrid Search” and “We Are Counties Microsite” substantially overlap with the current consultant role; keep these bullets more outcome-focused to avoid repeating responsibilities.
- “Advocacy Video Series” overlaps with multiple NACo roles; emphasize what was new, scaled, or sustained rather than general production/distribution tasks.

items.title: Coleman DAVIS
items.subtitle: Digital Platform & Communications Systems Leader
items.content: Senior digital leader with 12+ years of experience building the platforms, governance models and content operations behind high-volume public-sector communications. Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics infrastructure, editorial systems, multimedia production and AI-enabled user experiences for complex, mission-driven organizations.

items.title: Email
items.content: coleman@colemanpdavis.com

items.title: Website
items.content: https://colemanpdavis.com/

items.title: Core Competencies
items.content: Enterprise website modernization • Digital governance & editorial systems • Analytics and reporting infrastructure • Multi-channel communications operations • AI-enabled search and content experiences • Workflow automation and platform integration • Advocacy and public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Consult a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, current role with clear strategic + technical scope, but it reads broad and overlaps heavily with your prior NACo entries and Recent Projects. Tighten it around consultant-level outcomes, transformation work, and what is new since returning.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper scope statement: “Advise NACo on digital strategy, Drupal platform enhancements, content operations, and AI-enabled discovery for enterprise communications.”
- Replace generic verbs with outcome-oriented phrasing: “Redesigned workflows and analytics for coordinated cross-channel communications” instead of “Build and refine digital systems…”
- Consolidate web/CMS bullets: combine microsites, front-end implementation, and troubleshooting into one bullet focused on delivered platform improvements.
- Add measurable signals where possible: number of sites/pages supported, campaign launches, toolkit downloads, search accuracy gains, time saved, or stakeholder teams enabled.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Governance, usability and operational best practices” repeats themes already covered in Director of Digital Media; only keep if tied to a distinct consulting outcome.
- The AI search and microsite bullets may duplicate Recent Projects; summarize here and let the project section hold the detail.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with good scale metrics; it should be tightened to emphasize enterprise ownership and outcomes over channel-by-channel description. Focus this item on transformation, systems, and leadership since older NACo roles already cover newsletters/video execution.

Suggested edit
- Open with a sharper summary: “Directed NACo’s digital media function, leading web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget for a high-volume public-sector communications operation.”
- Rewrite bullets to foreground outcomes: “Led redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page Drupal website serving 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Combine channel oversight into one concise bullet and add performance if available: email engagement growth, social growth, production volume, cost savings, or turnaround improvements.
- Tighten operations/analytics bullets: “Built enterprise analytics stack across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery, improving leadership reporting and decision-making”; “Established governance, publishing standards, and cross-department planning workflows.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Directed core digital communications channels” overlaps with the Associate Communications Director role.
- Video studio/buildout may overlap with older video-production bullets unless framed here as strategic capacity-building.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this entry reads broad and overlaps with the more senior NACo roles. Tighten it around executional leadership, channel ownership, and concrete scale so it adds distinct value.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite the lead to emphasize operational ownership: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications across web, email, social and video, scaling editorial coordination and advocacy messaging across teams.”
- Combine related bullets and sharpen verbs: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Make the video bullet more outcome-focused: “Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “helped improve” with direct contribution and, if possible, metrics: “Standardized editorial planning and publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams, improving consistency and turnaround time.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Led day-to-day digital communications operations” overlaps with Director of Digital Media; keep this role more execution-focused, less enterprise-level.
- Weekly video/update language also overlaps with the 2015–2018 role and footer project; avoid repeating “first” or “built” claims here.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it largely repeats the header and Core Competencies. Tighten it to emphasize higher-value leadership themes and avoid generic phrasing like “audience-focused content planning.”

Suggested edit:
- Replace with sharper, less repetitive bullets such as:
- Enterprise digital strategy and web modernization
- Editorial governance and content operations
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy communications
- Audience strategy and campaign storytelling
- Prefer “content operations” over “content planning” to better reflect your recent leadership scope.
- Use “cross-channel” instead of “multi-channel” for a cleaner, more current phrasing.
- If space allows, align wording to recent impact areas: governance, modernization, and campaign storytelling.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Editorial systems and governance” duplicate the header/Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” overlaps with “Advocacy and public-sector communications”; keep only one version across sections.

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a generic tool dump and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. For a topline skills line, emphasize higher-value, recent capabilities and group tools under outcomes-oriented themes.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as grouped, impact-oriented skills rather than a flat list: “Drupal and enterprise CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript, jQuery) • API integrations and workflow automation • SharePoint and Power Pages • Airtable-based operational systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Put Drupal/CMS modernization first; it aligns with the most recent and highest-impact work.
- Replace “technical execution” jargon with clearer phrasing like “front-end implementation” or “platform delivery.”
- If space allows, swap one tool item for a stronger capability: “structured content workflows” or “modular content architecture,” which better reflects recent project work.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This item duplicates much of “Technical + IT”; keep Topline Skills higher-level and let the technical section hold the full tool list.
- “AI-enabled search experiences” also appears in Core Competencies; keep it in only one place unless it is a signature differentiator.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization
items.content:
- GA4
- Microsoft Clarity
- Looker Studio
- Power BI
- BigQuery
- KPI design
- Leadership reporting
- SEO and performance analysis
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant skill cluster for recent leadership roles, but it overlaps heavily with “Core Competencies” and “Technical + IT.” Tighten it to emphasize decision-making impact and avoid reading like a duplicate tool list.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from pure tools to capability + outcome language, e.g. “Analytics strategy, dashboards and executive reporting.”
- Keep 5–7 items max; group tools together instead of listing every platform separately.
- Suggested rewrite:
- Analytics strategy & KPI framework design
- Executive dashboards and leadership reporting
- GA4, BigQuery, Looker Studio and Power BI
- User behavior analysis with Microsoft Clarity
- SEO, content performance and conversion optimization
- If you have metrics elsewhere, align wording to support them (e.g. reporting for 3.5M annual page views, 10,000+ page migration, 50+ publishers).

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Current wording duplicates “Analytics and reporting infrastructure” in Core Competencies.
- Tool list substantially repeats “Data, Analytics & Optimization” in Technical + IT; this section should feel more strategic, not identical.

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery
items.content:
- Video production and editing
- Livestreaming
- PTZ camera systems
- Studio operations
- Hybrid and virtual event production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads as a generic tool list and overlaps with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” elsewhere. Make it more senior and outcomes-oriented, reflecting recent leadership in studio buildout and event delivery.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to emphasize scope: **Multimedia Production, Studio Operations & Event Delivery**
- Replace generic bullets with tighter, higher-level phrasing:
- Broadcast-quality video production and post-production  
- Livestream and hybrid event production  
- PTZ camera and in-house studio operations  
- Virtual event workflows and technical delivery
- If space allows, add one impact cue in the skills intro or adjacent experience instead of here, e.g. “built NACo’s first in-house video studio.”
- Keep this section to capabilities only; save tools/software detail for “Technical + IT.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Livestreaming” and “video production” duplicate the Core Competencies line on multimedia/livestream operations.
- “Studio operations” is already supported by the Director of Digital Media bullet about building the in-house studio, so avoid repeating that accomplishment here.

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid, scannable list, but it’s too generic and duplicates the “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” topline skills section. Since Drupal is central to recent roles, this item should better signal depth and recency or be tightened to avoid repetition.

Suggested edit:
- Reorder by relevance/recency: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages** is fine, but consider adding context: **Drupal (enterprise migrations, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, make Drupal more outcome-oriented: **Drupal (10,000+ page migration; campaign microsites)** to reinforce recent impact.
- Keep naming consistent with the rest of the CV; use either plain platform names everywhere or add short qualifiers consistently.
- If this section is meant to be purely technical, consider dropping the title to **CMS Platforms** for concision.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely repeats **Topline Skills → Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; consider removing one instance or using this version to add brief specialization/context.
- Drupal experience is already strongly evidenced in recent work bullets, so avoid overloading multiple sections with the same undifferentiated list.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical stack, but it reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution.” For a senior, recent-profile CV, this item should emphasize implementation depth and modern tooling rather than basic languages alone.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from raw languages to applied capability: “Front-end implementation (HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery) • API and tag management integrations • Edge/serverless scripting (Cloudflare Workers) • Deployment automation (GitHub Actions)”
- Consider dropping version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless used consistently elsewhere; “HTML/CSS/JavaScript” is cleaner.
- If accurate, add scope or outcome in adjacent experience bullets instead of here, e.g., “used for Drupal microsites, analytics tagging, and workflow automation.”
- Put the strongest, more current tools first: “Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • HTML/CSS/JavaScript • jQuery”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills.
- “Google Tag Manager” may fit better under Analytics/Optimization if space is tight.

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this reads as a generic software list rather than evidence of workflow leadership. It also overlaps with “Workflow automation and platform integration” in Core Competencies and “Airtable systems / Workflow automation” in Topline Skills.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to emphasize business value, e.g. **Workflow Automation & Collaboration Tools**.
- Tighten and group by function: **Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier | Jira, Asana, Trello, Basecamp | Slack, Teams**
- Put the strongest/recent tools first; keep only platforms you’ve actively used in recent roles.
- If space allows, add a light qualifier instead of just listing tools: **Workflow automation, project coordination, and cross-team collaboration using Airtable, Power Automate, Zapier, Jira, Asana, Slack, and Teams**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Airtable and workflow automation already appear in Topline Skills/Core Competencies; avoid repeating the same phrasing.
- Jira/Asana/Trello/Basecamp are similar; consider trimming to the 2–3 most credible/current platforms.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful platform list, but it reads as a generic software inventory. Since email leadership already appears strongly in recent NACo roles, this item should emphasize system depth or be tightened to avoid over-weighting older/basic tools.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Reorder by likely enterprise relevance/recency: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add scope qualifiers instead of just names: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys (campaign automation, segmentation) • Higher Logic (member email/community engagement) • Mailchimp (newsletter operations)**
- Keep only platforms you can discuss at implementation/administration level; otherwise trim to the 1–2 strongest systems.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Email/channel leadership is already covered in recent NACo experience, so avoid adding broad claims here like “managed newsletters” or “multi-channel campaigns.”
- “Engagement” may overlap with Core Competencies’ “Multi-channel communications operations”; keep this item platform-specific.

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item is too generic and largely duplicates the stronger “Analytics, Insights & Optimization” topline skills and recent NACo experience. Use it to sharpen technical specificity, not repeat broad capabilities.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Analytics & Optimization Tools**
- Tighten to tool-first phrasing: **GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • BigQuery • Looker Studio • Power BI • Google Search Console • A/B testing**
- Replace vague **Dashboarding** with a more concrete term such as **KPI reporting** or **Executive dashboards**
- If accurate, add one implementation-level skill that shows depth, e.g. **event tracking strategy**, **data visualization**, or **SEO analysis**

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps heavily with **Topline Skills: Analytics, Insights & Optimization**; consider keeping strategy terms there and reserving this section for platforms/tools only.
- GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery are already reinforced in the 2022–2024 role, so avoid repeating broader phrases like “analytics infrastructure” here.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is still broad and reads like a setup role rather than showing concrete contributions. Tighten it around team-building, platform work, and recurring content production with any available scale metrics.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground advancement and outcomes: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team and improve workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Split the second sentence into clearer achievements: website refresh, livestream/video production, and informal supervision.
- Add measurable scope if possible: number of livestreams, frequency/views of weekly videos, site traffic during refresh, or size of team supported.
- Replace softer phrasing like “high-impact” and “day-to-day guidance” with specifics such as “produced X livestreams and weekly video briefings” and “mentored 1 digital media associate.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Avoid repeating “weekly advocacy video update,” which is already covered in the 2018–2022 role.
- “Strengthening workflows across web, email, social” overlaps with later operations/governance entries; keep this version focused on early team formation and production.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry with a credible “first podcast” achievement, but it reads generic and overlaps with later multimedia/digital roles. Tighten it to emphasize coordination, cross-functional support, and the podcast launch as the clearest outcome.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite to foreground the strongest accomplishment: “Supported county innovation and policy initiatives through research coordination, program support, and digital communications.”
- Make the podcast launch the second sentence and sharpen ownership: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading planning, scripting, and production.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials” with a more specific verb: “Produced digital and multimedia content to support program and policy communications.”
- If possible, add one measurable detail: number of episodes launched, stakeholder groups supported, or projects/campaigns coordinated.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Digital content production and multimedia” overlaps with later Digital Media Manager / Producer and Associate Communications Director entries; keep this item lighter and more foundational.
- Avoid overstating digital leadership here since stronger, more recent leadership evidence appears in 2018–2024 roles.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but reads a bit dated and overlaps heavily with “Multimedia production and livestream operations” in Core Competencies and “Multimedia Production & Event Delivery” in Topline Skills. Make it more tool-specific and execution-focused, not a third summary of the same capability.

Suggested edit:
